original_question: For each integer k >= 3, determine the infimum alpha(k) such that every graph G of order n = Omega(k^alpha) with lambda(G) > lambda(S^+_{n,k}) contains a cycle C_{2k+2}.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 2 of arXiv:2305.10290 ('A refined version of Nikiforov’s even cycle conjecture'); the survey explicitly points to the full underlying formulation in Li–Ning [94], where it appears as Problem 29 in Section 3 ('Concluding remarks').
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful target. It has the right quantifier pattern ('for each integer k >= 3'), the right extremal comparison graph S^+_{n,k}, the right spectral threshold λ(G) > λ(S^+_{n,k}), the right conclusion (existence of C_{2k+2}), and the right refined goal of determining an infimum exponent α(k) that measures how large n must be relative to k. This matches the refined problem recorded in the paper rather than a broader neighboring conjecture.
missing_details: The paper treats graphs as simple, undirected, and unweighted; that ambient graph-theoretic setting should be stated explicitly for a stand-alone question.
The notation λ(H) should be defined as the adjacency spectral radius, i.e. the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of H.
The extremal graph S_{n,k} should be defined as K_k ∨ (n-k)K_1, the join of a k-clique and an independent set of size n-k.
The graph S^+_{n,k} should be defined explicitly as the graph obtained from S_{n,k} by adding one edge inside the independent set of size n-k.
The order condition n = Ω(k^α) should be unpacked exactly as in the source: there exists a constant c > 0, independent of k and n, such that n >= c k^α.
It should be explicit that 'contains a C_{2k+2}' means contains a cycle of length 2k+2 as a subgraph, not necessarily an induced cycle.
The infimum should be stated to be over real exponents α, with α allowed to depend on k (written α = α(k)).
For full paper-faithfulness, it helps to note that this is presented as a refined version of Nikiforov’s conjecture, isolating the hidden dependence of 'sufficiently large n' on k.
refined_question: For each fixed integer k >= 3, determine the infimum real number α(k) such that there exists a constant c > 0, independent of k and n, with the following property: every simple undirected graph G on n vertices satisfying n >= c k^{α(k)} and λ(G) > λ(S^+_{n,k}) contains a cycle C_{2k+2}, where λ(H) denotes the adjacency spectral radius of H, S_{n,k} := K_k ∨ (n-k)K_1, and S^+_{n,k} is obtained from S_{n,k} by adding one edge between two vertices of the independent set.
justification: The draft is not aiming at the already-solved extremal statement that the C_{2k+2}-free graph of maximum spectral radius is S^+_{n,k}; instead, it asks for the quantitative dependence hidden inside the phrase 'n sufficiently large relative to k'. That is exactly the refined open problem singled out in the survey as Problem 2 and stated with full notation in the cited source as Problem 29. The surrounding paragraph before Problem 29 supplies the missing definitions of S_{n,k} and S^+_{n,k}, and the parenthetical clause in Problem 29 gives the exact meaning of n = Ω(k^α). The paragraph immediately after Problem 29 explains why this refinement matters: for example, proving the conjecture in a form such as n = Ω(k^2) would help extend tight spectral conditions for even cycles beyond the currently known short- and long-cycle ranges.
